title: Removing one of two equal values from a composite map
summary: Removing one of two equal values now succeeds and leaves the second mapping intact. A second removal through the same public values view throws UnsupportedOperationException with that mapping still present.

change.description: The merged collection stops after its first successful removal. The PR identifies the single-occurrence rule for Collection.remove(Object).

notes: The first removal on the parent had already mutated the first backing map when it threw. The merged live view also exposed a previously shadowed value after the winning mapping was removed.
The same caller on Spring 7.1.0 reproduced all four observations, including the exception with b=x intact on the second removal. Removal through a collection is optional.
